**Visual Analysis:**

- **Affected part**: Wheat head (spike)
- **Key features**:
  - Dark/black sooty masses replacing grain kernels throughout the spikelets
  - Glumes are partially intact/gaping open, revealing dark spore material inside
  - Awns are still present and pale/straw-colored
  - The entire grain tissue appears replaced by dark powdery/granular spore masses
  - Head structure mostly preserved, but interiors of spikelets filled with dark material

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Loose Smut** (*Ustilago tritici*): Replaces grain tissue with dark powdery teliospore masses; glumes become vestigial or spread open exposing the dark masses; awns remain intact. This matches the image well — the dark masses are visible within/replacing the grain, with pale awns still present.
- **Dwarf Bunt**: Also produces dark masses but kernels are replaced by rounded "bunt balls" enclosed within glumes; plants are notably stunted; not obviously matching here.
- **Head Scab**: Would show bleached/tan spikelets, possibly with pink sporulation — not dark masses.
- **Stem Rust/Wheat Stem Rust**: Produces pustules on stems/leaves, not dark grain replacement.

The image strongly shows complete replacement of grain tissue with dark spore masses while awns remain, which is the hallmark of **Loose Smut**.
